skill.name: cloudflare
skill.description: Use Cloudflare platform references to plan, build, configure, and troubleshoot Workers, Pages, storage, AI, networking, security, and infrastructure-as-code projects.
skill.summary: Build and troubleshoot Cloudflare projects with focused product guidance and reference-driven examples.
skill.author: cloudflare

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily a large Cloudflare reference bundle with many static matches caused by documentation examples, placeholders, and product configuration snippets. A small number of command-execution examples remain security-sensitive because users or agents could copy them into real environments, but no hidden malware, prompt injection, credential exfiltration intent, or auto-executing installer behavior was found. Static review was capped at 400/2983 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 2583 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Pipe-to-shell installation example in sandbox guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-shell command with explicit download, checksum verification, and reviewed installation steps.

remediation.issue: Privileged tunnel service examples can alter host persistence.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear warnings and require manual approval before running systemd or sudo commands from the references.

remediation.issue: Dynamic execution examples may be copied into application code.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer safer APIs, constrain inputs, and label exec or eval examples as non-production demonstrations.

remediation.issue: Many examples mention secrets, certificates, tokens, and environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholder values clearly fake and remind users never to paste real credentials into prompts or source files.

content.value_statement: Cloudflare projects span many products, APIs, and configuration formats. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code choose the right Cloudflare service and use targeted references for implementation.
actual_capabilities: Select suitable Cloudflare products for storage, compute, AI, networking, security, and analytics tasks.
Guide Workers, Pages, Durable Objects, KV, D1, R2, Queues, and Workflows implementation work.
Reference Cloudflare configuration patterns for Wrangler, Terraform, Pulumi, tunnels, and bindings.
Explain common gotchas for product limits, compatibility dates, deployment flows, and runtime behavior.
Support troubleshooting for Cloudflare APIs, edge applications, storage integrations, and platform features.
Encourage checking current Cloudflare documentation before using limits, pricing, or API signatures.
limitations: The bundled references may become outdated and should not replace current Cloudflare documentation.
Some examples use placeholders or demonstration credentials that users must replace safely.
The skill does not grant access to a Cloudflare account or execute deployments by itself.
Security-sensitive commands and infrastructure changes still require user review before use.

use_cases.title: Choose a Cloudflare architecture
use_cases.description: Compare Workers, Pages, Durable Objects, KV, D1, R2, Queues, and related services for a new application design.

use_cases.title: Configure deployments and infrastructure
use_cases.description: Draft Wrangler, Terraform, Pulumi, tunnel, binding, and environment setup guidance for Cloudflare projects.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot platform behavior
use_cases.description: Find product-specific gotchas for runtime errors, storage behavior, networking issues, and deployment failures.

prompt_templates.title: Pick the right Cloudflare product
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to build [describe app]. Which Cloudflare products should I use, and why?

prompt_templates.title: Create a Workers implementation plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me implement [feature] on Cloudflare Workers. Include bindings, Wrangler configuration, and deployment steps.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Cloudflare deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this Cloudflare issue: [error or symptom]. Ask for missing context, then check likely product-specific causes.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Cloudflare architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Cloudflare architecture for security, reliability, cost, and operational risks: [architecture details].

output_examples.input: Which storage option should I use for user profiles and uploaded images?
output: Use D1 or Durable Objects for relational profile data that needs queries or coordination.
Use R2 for uploaded images and store object keys in the profile records.
Use KV only for cached or low-consistency lookup data.

output_examples.input: Help me deploy a Pages app with a Worker API.
output_examples.output: A useful response would separate the Pages build settings, Worker routes, Wrangler bindings, environment variables, and deployment verification steps.

output_examples.input: My Worker cannot reach a private database.
output_examples.output: A useful response would check Hyperdrive, Workers VPC, tunnel options, secret configuration, egress requirements, and runtime error details.

best_practices: Verify current Cloudflare documentation before using limits, pricing, API signatures, or compatibility flags.
Keep secrets in Cloudflare-managed secret stores or bindings, not in source files or prompts.
Test Cloudflare configuration changes in a staging account or preview environment before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API tokens, certificates, private keys, or database URLs into prompts or examples.
Do not run shell commands from examples without reading and adapting them for your environment.
Do not assume a reference snippet is production-ready without reviewing security, permissions, and error handling.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy Cloudflare resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Any deployment still requires tool access, credentials, and user approval.

faq.question: Can it replace Cloudflare documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is a reference aid. Current Cloudflare documentation remains the source of truth for limits, pricing, and APIs.

faq.question: Which Cloudflare products does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Workers, Pages, KV, D1, R2, Durable Objects, Workers AI, Vectorize, Queues, Tunnels, security products, and infrastructure tools.

faq.question: Is it useful for Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude Code can use the skill to locate Cloudflare references while editing, reviewing, or troubleshooting project files.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes references for WAF, DDoS, bot management, API Shield, Turnstile, secrets, and secure configuration patterns.

faq.question: What should I verify before using generated commands?
faq.answer: Verify account IDs, zone IDs, permissions, secret handling, target environments, and whether the command changes shared infrastructure.
